nodes.title: STEP 1a - READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
## How to make a picture

1. In **STEP 7** type what you want to see - how she looks in the **physical** box, everything else in the other box.
2. Press the blue **Run** button, top right.
3. Wait 15-60 seconds. The picture(s) show up in **STEP 12**.

Every picture is archived automatically to `output/freedom_archive/` (the **auto_save** switch on STEP 12), so nothing you make is ever lost. STEP 12 is where you send the *keepers* somewhere of your own: click **Save Image** for a single picture, or tick the ones you want and click **Save Selected Images**. **Set User Save Folder** chooses where those copies go.

That's it. Everything else is already set up. The steps run left to right, 1 to 12. The last grey group, **BEHIND THE SCENES**, is plumbing - never touch it.

### If you want to change something
- **Different look / model:** click the file name in STEP 1.
- **Her face on or off:** STEP 2, the face source switch. Switched off, the same picture is painted with a generic person instead.
- **Which face:** STEP 3b, the Face Shelf.
- **Portrait Master dials and presets:** STEP 4.
- **Her face, extra passes:** STEP 3c repeats the face picked in STEP 3b, only when STEP 2 is trained_face. Its three passes (Face Lora Stack pass 1, pass 2 and pass 3) start ON at 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.1.
- **Add-on LoRAs (general stack):** STEP 6 works in both face modes, never loads a face, and starts with three rows and grows to twelve with **+ Add LoRA**. It only lists LoRAs that match this checkpoint. (Emotions, expression\_helper and Hands zib are NOT SDXL - they are Flux / Krea / Z-Image LoRAs and will not appear here or work with bigLust or Pony.)
- **Wider or taller, or how many:** STEP 9.
- **New random picture, same idea:** just press Run again.
- **Keep the same picture, tweak wording:** on **STEP 10** set *control_after_generate* to `fixed`, change a few words in STEP 7, Run.
- **Repaint her face on or off:** STEP 11, the switch.

nodes.title: STEP 1b - the art model
widgets_values:
**STEP 1 - the art model**

This opens the 'brain' that knows how to paint - **bigLust**, a photo-real model made for adult images.

It feeds three things to the rest of the recipe: the painter, the part that reads your words, and the part that turns the result into a normal picture.

**You touch this only** to switch models - click the file name to pick lustify, CyberRealistic Pony, etc.

nodes.title: STEP 1c  -  CheckpointLoaderSimple  -  Pick the art model
STEP 2a  -  FreedomFaceSource  -  Face source switch (trained / random / off)
STEP 3a - pick her face
widgets_values:
**Pick her face**

This is the shelf of every face you've trained. Click a picture to put that person's face - or face and body - onto whatever gets painted below. Each trained person shows up as two cards: one for face-only, one for face + body.

**The FACE ON / FACE OFF switch.** At the top of the shelf is a button that reads **FACE ON** in green. It decides whether this whole step does anything at all. Click it once and it turns red and reads **FACE OFF**.

**What FACE OFF really means.** The picture gets painted exactly as if this step were not in the workflow at all. Her face is not applied, and her trigger word is left out of your prompt as well. (A trigger word is the made-up word her training gave her, something like `br1tany woman`. It is the word that tells the art model to draw her and not a stranger.) So with the switch off, nothing about her reaches the picture - not her face, and not her name.

**Your pick is not lost.** The card you clicked stays clicked, just greyed out, and switching back on brings her straight back at the same strength. That is the difference between this switch and the **None** button beside it: **None** forgets who you picked, while the switch only pauses her.

**Two buttons, one switch.** You can flip it from the button on the shelf, or from the small toggle on the node itself just above the shelf, which reads **face ON** / **face OFF**. They are wired together, so moving either one moves both. You never have to wonder which one is in charge.

**When to use it.** Turn her off to try a new prompt, a new pose, or a different art model on a generic person first, so her face isn't pulling the picture around while you experiment. Then turn her back on and make the real one.

The **strength** slider is how much of her face this shelf loads - **0.4 by default**. STEP 3c, just below, adds the same face three more times at **0.3, 0.2 and 0.1**, so together she gets **1.0** (0.4 Face Shelf + 0.3 Face Lora Stack pass 1 + 0.2 Face Lora Stack pass 2 + 0.1 Face Lora Stack pass 3). The **Current** box at the top of STEP 3b and of STEP 3c shows the live total. In the 2026-09-25 tests, totals of 1.6 and above broke the picture.

**Refresh** picks up any face you've just finished training without restarting anything.

STEP 6a - general LoRA stack (both face modes)
widgets_values:
**General LoRA stack - trained face AND random face**

A LoRA is a small add-on file that teaches the art model one specific thing - a clothing item, a pose, a style - on top of what it already knows. This stack works in **both** face modes (STEP 2 = trained_face or random_face). It **never** loads a trained face: files in the `faces/` folder are left out of its list and refused if typed in. Her face is loaded by STEP 3b (the face shelf, one pass) and STEP 3c (extra passes, trained face only).

Four rows are always there. Tick a row on, pick a LoRA from its dropdown, and set its **strength** (0.8 is a safe starting point - higher can overpower the picture). A row that is ticked on but has no LoRA picked does nothing. The **X** on a row empties it; the row itself stays.

**All OFF** and **All ON** at the top switch every row at once. The green one shows which way the rows are set; both are gray when some rows are on and some are off.

The list only shows LoRAs made for the art model picked in STEP 1. After adding a new LoRA file, or changing STEP 1's model, click **Refresh list**.

You will not see any of her trained faces in this list - those live in STEP 3b and STEP 3c, so you can't load the wrong one here by mistake.

nodes.title: STEP 6c  -  FreedomLoraStack  -  General LoRA stack (trained face + random face, never her face)
STEP 7a - what you want
widgets_values:
**What you want - STEP 7c to 7f**

**SUMMARY SIGNAL (STEP 7c)** - page 1 of the prompt. The art model sums up the first 75 places of the prompt and keeps that summary in mind for the whole picture. The box starts with the model's own text for the model picked in STEP 1 (CyberRealistic Pony's score tags; nothing for bigLust), put in and taken out by itself when you switch models. Type your most important few words after it. The counter shows how many places are left; typing past page 1 is refused.

**SCENE PROMPT (STEP 7d)** - pose, action, scene, camera, lighting, style.
**PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION PROMPT (STEP 7e)** - how she looks: body, face, hair, skin, clothing.

Type in each box. Plain words or tags are fine. **Then press that box's big green button, "Update the FINAL COMBINED PROMPT".** Nothing updates by itself.

**FINAL COMBINED PROMPT (STEP 7f)** - read-only. It shows exactly what goes to the engine at Run, in this order: the Summary Signal, her trigger word (or Portrait Master's words), Physical Description, Scene. Its watcher line says when a box has changed since its green button was last pressed. The Prompt Watcher under it shows what the engine got on the last run.

**If you picked someone on STEP 3b's Face Shelf**, her trigger word goes in automatically (it arrives from STEP 5). In random-face mode Portrait Master writes its words at Run, so the final box shows a marker in their place until then.

**Scene and Physical each have their own shelf**, above the box: the dial walks your saved ones, the window shows the one you are on, and the buttons are **Load, Save (overwrite), Save as, Create new, Rename, Delete**. Any saved look can be paired with any saved scene.

Saved in `user/default/freedom_physical_slots.json` and `freedom_scene_slots.json`.

nodes.title: STEP 9a - size & how many
widgets_values:
**Size & how many**

Shape + how many at once. Default **1216 x 832** (wide, SDXL's native size - steadiest).

Presets: 1216x832 wide - 1024x512 wide letterbox - 832x1216 tall - 1024x1024 square - 1344x768 HD wide

1024x512 is a thinner letterbox but at 512 height bigLust can sometimes double a subject; 1216x832 is the safe default.

STEP 10a - the actual painting
widgets_values:
**The actual painting**

This is where the picture gets made. It takes the painter (STEP 1), your want / don't-want (STEPS 4-5) and the blank canvas (STEP 6), and cleans up random noise into an image over **26 passes**.

- **seed** = the random starting point. Same seed + same words = same picture.
- **control_after_generate**: `randomize` = new picture each Run; `fixed` = keep tweaking the same one.
- Leave steps / cfg / sampler as they are - they're tuned for bigLust.

STEP 11a - every FaceDetailer dial explained
widgets_values:
**STEP 11 - FaceDetailer (face repaint) - repaint the face as her**

When a picture shows her whole body, her face ends up tiny - sometimes only about
100 pixels across. But her face was trained on big head-and-shoulders photos, around
1000 pixels across. A face that small has no room for the details that make her look
like *her*, so she comes out looking like a generic person.

This step fixes that. It finds the face in the finished picture, cuts it out, blows it
up to a size her face model understands, paints it again using **the same face model and
the same words** that made the picture, then shrinks it back down and blends it in. The
rest of the picture is never touched.

### The ON / OFF switch

The small box to the left is the switch. **true = ON**, and the face gets repainted.
That is the normal setting. Click it to **false = OFF** and the picture comes out exactly
the way STEP 10 painted it - the repainting does not run at all, so it costs no time.

---

## Every dial, in plain words

Our value is shown in brackets where we have set one.

### Group 1 - how big the face gets blown up

- **guide_size (1024)** - the size the face is blown up to before repainting. 1024 is
  what her face was trained at, which is why it is set here.
- **guide_size_for (bbox)** - what that size is measured against. **bbox** means the face
  box itself. **crop_region** means the whole cut-out including the hair and neck around it.
  On bbox the face reaches the target size; on crop_region it ends up smaller.
- **max_size (1024)** - a ceiling on the blown-up cut-out, so a big close-up cannot grow
  into something your graphics card chokes on. Watch this one: when it bites, *it* decides
  the real size, not guide_size.

### Group 2 - the repaint itself (this is a small painter of its own)

- **seed** - the starting randomness for the repaint. Fix it and the same face comes back
  every time; randomize it and you get a different attempt each run.
- **control_after_generate** - what the seed does after each run: stay fixed, go up, go
  down, or randomize.
- **steps (26)** - how many passes the repaint takes. More is slower and usually finer.
- **cfg (6)** - how hard the repaint is pushed to obey the words. Too high and the face
  goes harsh and over-baked.
- **sampler_name (dpmpp_2m)** - which painting method it uses.
- **scheduler (karras)** - how the noise is stepped down across those steps.
- **denoise (0.15)** - how much of the existing face may change. Low keeps what was there;
  high redraws freely. Past about 0.6 the new face can stop matching the body.

### Group 3 - blending it back in

- **feather (8)** - how soft the edge is where the new face is pasted back. It blurs the
  mask by this amount. 0 gives a hard cut-out edge you can see.
- **noise_mask (on)** - repaint only inside the face mask rather than the whole cut-out.
  Normally on.

### Group 4 - finding the face in the first place

- **bbox_threshold (0.5)** - how sure the finder must be before it calls something a face.
  Raise it and it only accepts obvious faces; lower it and it starts finding faces in
  patterns and shadows.
- **bbox_dilation (10)** - grows the found box outwards by this many pixels, so the jaw and
  hairline are included rather than cut off at the skin.
- **bbox_crop_factor (3.0)** - how much extra picture is cut out around the box. Bigger
  takes in more neck and hair, blends more smoothly, and is slower.
- **drop_size (10)** - ignore any found face smaller than this across. Stops it wasting a
  full repaint on a face in the far background.

### Group 5 - when to skip the work

- **force_inpaint (off)** - off means "if the face is already bigger than guide_size, leave

  further and costs proportionally more time.

socket. SAM would trace the exact outline of the face instead of using a rectangle. There
is no SAM model on this machine - the `models/sams` folder does not exist - so the socket
is empty and all six of these are ignored no matter what you set them to.

- **inpaint_model** - turn on only if the model loaded is a true inpainting model. Wrong
  setting here gives a smeared patch.

  painting, as opposed to `feather` which softens it when pasting back.

  memory, at the cost of speed. For emergencies on a small card.

widgets_values_named.text:
**STEP 11 - FaceDetailer (face repaint) - repaint the face as her**

When a picture shows her whole body, her face ends up tiny - sometimes only about
100 pixels across. But her face was trained on big head-and-shoulders photos, around
1000 pixels across. A face that small has no room for the details that make her look
like *her*, so she comes out looking like a generic person.

This step fixes that. It finds the face in the finished picture, cuts it out, blows it
up to a size her face model understands, paints it again using **the same face model and
the same words** that made the picture, then shrinks it back down and blends it in. The
rest of the picture is never touched.

### The ON / OFF switch

The small box to the left is the switch. **true = ON**, and the face gets repainted.
That is the normal setting. Click it to **false = OFF** and the picture comes out exactly
the way STEP 10 painted it - the repainting does not run at all, so it costs no time.

---

## Every dial, in plain words

Our value is shown in brackets where we have set one.

### Group 1 - how big the face gets blown up

- **guide_size (1024)** - the size the face is blown up to before repainting. 1024 is
  what her face was trained at, which is why it is set here.
- **guide_size_for (bbox)** - what that size is measured against. **bbox** means the face
  box itself. **crop_region** means the whole cut-out including the hair and neck around it.
  On bbox the face reaches the target size; on crop_region it ends up smaller.
- **max_size (1024)** - a ceiling on the blown-up cut-out, so a big close-up cannot grow
  into something your graphics card chokes on. Watch this one: when it bites, *it* decides
  the real size, not guide_size.

### Group 2 - the repaint itself (this is a small painter of its own)

- **seed** - the starting randomness for the repaint. Fix it and the same face comes back
  every time; randomize it and you get a different attempt each run.
- **control_after_generate** - what the seed does after each run: stay fixed, go up, go
  down, or randomize.
- **steps (26)** - how many passes the repaint takes. More is slower and usually finer.
- **cfg (6)** - how hard the repaint is pushed to obey the words. Too high and the face
  goes harsh and over-baked.
- **sampler_name (dpmpp_2m)** - which painting method it uses.
- **scheduler (karras)** - how the noise is stepped down across those steps.
- **denoise (0.15)** - how much of the existing face may change. Low keeps what was there;
  high redraws freely. Past about 0.6 the new face can stop matching the body.

### Group 3 - blending it back in

- **feather (8)** - how soft the edge is where the new face is pasted back. It blurs the
  mask by this amount. 0 gives a hard cut-out edge you can see.
- **noise_mask (on)** - repaint only inside the face mask rather than the whole cut-out.
  Normally on.

### Group 4 - finding the face in the first place

- **bbox_threshold (0.5)** - how sure the finder must be before it calls something a face.
  Raise it and it only accepts obvious faces; lower it and it starts finding faces in
  patterns and shadows.
- **bbox_dilation (10)** - grows the found box outwards by this many pixels, so the jaw and
  hairline are included rather than cut off at the skin.
- **bbox_crop_factor (3.0)** - how much extra picture is cut out around the box. Bigger
  takes in more neck and hair, blends more smoothly, and is slower.
- **drop_size (10)** - ignore any found face smaller than this across. Stops it wasting a
  full repaint on a face in the far background.

widgets_values:
**STEP 4a hints - the two nationality settings (Portrait Master's Base Character, STEP 4c)**

**nationality_1 and nationality_2.** These say where the person is from. With **one** set (the other on "-"), Portrait Master writes it plainly, for example "togolese woman". With **both** set, it writes a mix of the two. In this workflow both are on "random", so it always picks two.

**The mix used to need Prompt Control.** Portrait Master writes a two-nationality mix as "[togolese:south sudanese:0.5]". Only the add-on Prompt Control understood that as "use the first nationality for half of the drawing, then the second", and the **nationality_mix** slider set where that switch happened. Portrait Master's own instructions call this feature experimental.

**Your decision (29 September 2026): keep it simple.** Prompt Control only really affected this one nationality setting, so it was removed from ComfyUI. Now:
- a two-nationality mix is written in plain words, for example "togolese and south sudanese". STEP 7d does this on Portrait Master's text only; Portrait Master's own files are not changed, and your own STEP 7 boxes are never rewritten.
- the **nationality_mix** slider no longer does anything, so it is hidden on Base Character.

Why this matters: the words decide the picture. Plain words are read the same way every time; the old bracket was only understood with Prompt Control installed.

Record: logs/prompt_control_removed_2026-09-29.md
